newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic says first Reveal implants done.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic says first Reveal implants done.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said the first human implantations of its Reveal insertable loop recorder were accomplished by surgeons in Canada.

The Reveal is the world's first implantable heart monitor designed to be inserted under the skin in the chest area to record the heart's rhythm during symptoms, such as fainting, that may suggest heartbeat disorder, Medtronic said.
Reveal recorders were implanted in two women, ages 23 and 77, and a 71-year-old man, on February 4, at the London Health Sciences Centre at the University of Western Ontario.
All three patients have a history of fainting, the cause of which has not been determined by available diagnostic testing, said the medical technology company.

The Reveal recorder continually records a subcutaneous electrocardiogram. When symptoms occur, the patient uses a hand-held activator to store a segment of the ECG into the device's memory for later analysis by a physician.

The device is about two inches long, three-fourths of an inch wide, and a quarter of an inch thick. It has an estimated minimum life of one year after insertion. Electrodes that sense the heart's activity are on the surface of the device, so no wire heart connections are needed, Medtronic said.
More implantations will take place in Canada, Europe, Africa and the Middle East, although the device is not available in the United States, Medtronic said.
